title: Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization-Mass Spectrometric Imaging (MALDI-MSI)
author: Ian M. Tamayo
materials: Imaging data are opened via SCILS software, where they are “Exported to METASPACE” in form of .imzML and .ibd files.

Enable the MALDI system. External calibration of instrument is performed using FlexMix (Thermo), resulting in mass measurement accuracy within 1 ppm within the m/z range 50-700. Image data is acquired using ‘MALDI Injector Software’.
Imaging data are opened via ImageInsight software (MALDI-Q Exactive). The data are converted into the form of .imzML and .ibd files in the centroid mode.

steps.title: Prepare Slide for MALDI-15T-FTICR-MSI
steps.instruction: Remove slide(s) from the HTX sprayer, remount them in the MTP slide Adapter II (Bruker Catalog #8235380), and load them into the MS instrument.

steps.title: Perform External Instrument Calibration
steps.instruction: Calibrate the MALDI-15T-FTICR-MSI (Bruker Daltonics) using TuneMix (Agilent, G1969-85010) via electrospray ionization (ESI) to achieve mass measurement accuracy within 1 ppm across the entire m/z range.

steps.title: Run Laser Imaging and Peak Picking
steps.instruction: Acquire image data using FlexImaging (v4.1, Bruker Daltonics), stepping the laser across the sample in 35 μm, 50 μm, or 75 μm increments, analyzing the sample in triplicate for each resolution.

substeps.instruction: Perform peak picking during the run to collect all ions with intensity > 1e5 and a signal-to-noise ratio > 1.

steps.title: Configure Positive-Ion Mode Parameters
steps.instruction: Optimize analyzer parameters for the MALDI-15T-FTICR-MSI in positive-ion mode.

substeps.instruction: Set analysis range to m/z 200-1500 with a resolution of 1M (corresponding to 140,000 at 400 m/z).
Use 200 shots at a frequency of 2,000 Hz to ablate material from one pixel position.

steps.title: Configure Negative-Ion Mode Parameters
steps.instruction: Optimize analyzer parameters for the MALDI-15T-FTICR-MSI in negative-ion mode.

substeps.instruction: Set analysis range to m/z 200-1500 with a resolution of 1M (corresponding to approx 140,000 at 400 m/z).
Use 100 shots at a frequency of 2,000 Hz to ablate material from one pixel position.

steps.title: Upload Data to METASPACE
steps.instruction: Upload .imzML and .ibd files to METASPACE (https://metaspace2020.eu/) and enter metadata according to the METASPACE template and requirements.

steps.title: Prepare Slide for MALDI-Q Exactive
steps.instruction: Remove the slide from the HTX sprayer and load it into the slide holder in the MALDI injector (SpectroGlyph).

steps.title: Initialize MALDI Source Vacuum
steps.instruction: Turn on the vacuum pump for the MALDI source.

steps.title: Adjust Pressure and Gate Wall
steps.instruction: Open the 'Gate Wall' between the MALDI and Q Exactive HF-X.

substeps.instruction: Adjust QE fore vacuum pressure to 1.5 mbar.

steps.title: Scan Sample with Laser
steps.instruction: Step the laser across the sample in 20 μm (routine) or 5 μm (regions of interest) increments, analyzing the sample in four replicated sections.

substeps.instruction: Perform peak picking during the run to collect all ions with intensity > 1e5 and a signal-to-noise ratio > 4.

steps.title: Configure Negative-Ion Mode (MALDI-Q Exactive)
steps.instruction: Optimize analyzer parameters for the MALDI-Q Exactive in negative-ion mode.

substeps.instruction: Set analysis range to m/z 70-700 with a resolution of 1M (corresponding to 120,000 at 200 m/z).
Set laser repetition rate to 1000 Hz.

steps.title: Upload Q Exactive Data to METASPACE
steps.instruction: Upload .imzML and .ibd files to METASPACE (https://metaspace2020.eu/) and enter metadata according to the METASPACE template and requirements.
